overview: Black plays 2...Qc7 before ...Nc6 or ...e6, the Accelerated Paulsen set-up, keeping options like ...a6, ...Nf6, ...Nc6. After 3.d4 cxd4 4.Nxd4 the game transposes to Paulsen or Taimanov-type positions, and White can also go for Maroczy bind with c4. Black has a half-open c-file and flexible development.

white_ideas.idea: Play d4 and Nxd4, then Nc3 and Be3 with an open Sicilian
Build a bind with c4 where possible

black_ideas.idea: Use the queen on c7 for ...Nc6, ...a6 and ...e6
Pressure the c-file and meet e4 with ...Nf6

typical_structures.structure: Open Sicilian with asymmetrical centre, Black with the c-file

character.notes: Paulsen set-ups are flexible and not necessarily forcing.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: A sound if slightly unusual move order.

structure.notes: Sicilian: asymmetrical centre and a half-open c-file.

approach.notes: A sideline that strong players do not often choose first; but a normal option.

level.notes: Sicilian understanding needed, theory is moderate.

sublines_that_differ.name: Maroczy Bind
sublines_that_differ.how: White avoids the open Sicilian and gets a bind

character.reason: Flexible Paulsen-type play, not clearly solid or sharp.

structure.reason: A Sicilian with a half-open c-file.

approach.reason: Less common but a respectable move order.
